notes: RLHF method lineage resolved cleanly: Christiano 2017 (reward modeling) -> Ziegler 2019 (first LM application) -> Stiennon 2020 (full recipe, InstructGPT template, six shared authors) -> RLHF 2022; PPO is the optimizer throughout. GPT-3 linked as substrate edge (fourth convergence; GPT-3 in-degree 2). Coeval drops: InstructGPT, Constitutional AI, Sparrow (all 2022); DPO (2023) post-dated. Substrate vs method edge distinction recorded in GPT-3 verification notes.

Policy-gradient spine resolved: REINFORCE 1992 -> policy gradient theorem 2000 -> TRPO 2015 -> PPO 2017, with GAE 2016 as the consumed advantage estimator. GAE Q2 corrected to pass on primary-source re-read (high-dimensional continuous control claim) BEFORE the clean single verdict application. INCIDENT (resolved): an attempted verdict re-application created duplicate nodes; graph was restored byte-exact from sync checkpoint 8d37e278 via the git blobs API (blob 439d311e, 1,420,955 bytes, verified 24 nodes/27 edges) and the PPO expansion was redone in a single application. Lesson: apply-verdicts is NOT idempotent - never re-apply to an evaluated expansion; correct verdicts before applying, or restore from checkpoint.

Transformer resolved to its two proximate enablers: seq2seq (the transduction template it re-architected) and Bahdanau attention (the mechanism it generalized to self-attention). Components of the block (ResNet, LayerNorm, Adam) treated as substrate and failed at directness, consistent with prior expansions. Coeval drops at the 2017 bound: ConvS2S and structured self-attentive embeddings - parallel answers the same season. Decomposable attention (2016) logged as multiples context: attention-without-recurrence existed for NLI, so the leap is full self-attention transduction, not attention itself.
